headline: A 2017 executive order calls for a broad federal report on the largest US trade deficits with other countries.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order directs the federal government to prepare a combined report on significant trade deficits, meaning cases where the US buys much more from a country than it sells to it. No summary was provided, so details such as who writes the report, its deadline, and what it must cover are not confirmed here. On its face, the order asks for a study. It does not by itself set new taxes, tariffs, or trade rules.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that handle trade policy
who_it_affects.how: They would likely be tasked with gathering trade data and writing the report.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed March 31, 2017; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
